r: The **greatest king** of the Vengi Chalukyas; ruled **43 years**
Defeated the **Rashtrakuta Krishna II** and the **Kalinga king Devendravarma**; expanded the kingdom
**Gunaka-Nallata, Parachakra Rama, Vallabha**, Vira Makaradhwaja, Ranaranga Sudraka, Dakshinadhipati

0.x: **Pandaranga = commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya**, of the **Vengi (Eastern) Chalukyas**.

r: One of **four Brahmin generals** (Pandaranga, Vinayaditya Sarma, Kadiyaraju, Rajaditya)
Subdued the **Boyas**; built **Pandurangapuram** and a Maheswara temple on **Pulicat lake**
The **first Telugu verse (padya) inscription**, in **Taruvoja** metre
Developed by **Vijayaditya III (Gunaga Vijayaditya)** on the lines of **Bezawada**; Pandaranga made it a strong fort after conquering the Boya kingdoms
**Court poet of Rajaraja Narendra**, who **patronised** him
Began the **Andhra Mahabharatamu** (c. 1045–65): **Adi, Sabha** and part of **Aranya** parvas – begun by the court poet, **not the king**, at Rajaraja Narendra's request (11th century)
The **earliest surviving Telugu literary work**, in **Champu** (verse + prose) style

1.x: **Telugu literature owes its origin to the (Eastern) Chalukyas** – the Vengi court turned Telugu into a literary language.
Narayana Bhattu and the Nandampudi grant
**Narayana Bhattu helped Nannaya** – a scholar sent to Vengi as the **Kalyani Chalukya** (Someshvara I) representative; title **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara**.
**Evidence: the Nandampudi grant (copper-plate inscription) of Rajaraja Narendra**.
**Donee of Nandampudi village = Narayana Bhattu**; **Nannaya composed** the grant.
**Korumelli** plates of Rajaraja Narendra – same scribe as Nandampudi.

r: **Pavuluri Ganitamu** – Telugu verse of **Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham**; first scientific text in Telugu
**First (complete) Telugu inscription of the Eastern Chalukyas**
Champakamala verse; half Telugu, half Sanskrit

2.x: **Built by Ammaraja I (Vishnuvardhana VI, 921–927)** – also called **Ammaraja Vishnuvardhana I** – whose title **Rajamahendra** gave the city its name.

r: Ammaraja I moved the capital from Vengi here – the "**cultural capital of the Andhras**"
Built in the time of the **Eastern Chalukyas**
Created in the **Madras Presidency in 1823**; split into Godavari and Krishna in 1859
**Ammaraja I** made it capital; Rajaraja Narendra ruled from it

2.x: **Kartikeya (Kumaraswamy) temple at Bezawada: Yuddhamalla**, recorded in his **Bezawada inscription**.
**Bezawada inscription = Yuddhamalla's reign** – the famous Telugu **Madhyakkara** verse record of **Yuddhamalla II** (10th c.), son of Talapa, ruling from **Chebrolu**.

r: **Brother of Pulakeshin II**; founded the **Chalukyas of Vengi**
**Pulakeshin II** took it after defeating the **Vishnukundins** (c. 616)
Kopparam plates (**631**) of Pulakeshin II call him **Yuvaraja**; Chipurupalli plates (**Vizianagaram**) of his **18th regnal year**
**Vishamasiddhi** ("conqueror of difficult places / forts"); also **Makaradhwaja**, Kamadeva, Parama Bhagavata
Branch of the **Badami Chalukyas**; initially **subordinates of Badami**
They were **not annexed by the Rashtrakutas** – they survived the long wars and merged into the **Chola** line

3.x: **Contemporaries in the south: the Pallavas** – Jayasimha I clashed with them; the Ikshvakus were earlier.

r: An **Eastern Chalukya** prince; ousted by Vishnuvardhana III, he set up a kingdom at **Yalamanchili**
Defeated by **Dhruva**, who married his daughter **Sheela Mahadevi**
**360 battles** (Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva); repelled **Krishna II** at Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru; court singer and dancer **Chellavva**, title **Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada**
**Kollabhiganda**; ruled **six months**; died at **Virajapuri** fighting Kalinga
**Chalukya Chandra**; with Chola help beat **Bayyalanambi** of Satyasraya (1006)
Crowned **1022**; married **Ammanga Devi** (Rajendra Chola's daughter); after **Koppam (1053)** accepted **Kalyani** suzerainty; titles **Kavyageetha Priyudu** (lover of poetry), Rajarajanarayana

3.x: **Succession war:** **Rajaraja Narendra** (son of Kundavai, backed by **Rajendra I**) vs **Vijayaditya VII** (son of Melama, backed by the Kalyani Jayasimha II); **Rajadhiraja I** won at **Dharanikota**, burnt **Kollipaka**, and was killed at **Koppam** by **Ahavamalla Someshwara**.
After **973** the main rival was the **Kalyani Chalukyas**.
The **Cholas kept close political and matrimonial ties with the Chalukyas of Vengi**.

**Rajendra Chalukya = Kulottunga I** (married **Madhurantaki**, daughter of **Rajendra II**) united the two lines – the first Chalukya-Chola king; the **Chalukya-Chola era / Mandalika Yugam** (1076–c.1210, Velanati Chodas) followed.
Andhra order: **Eastern Chalukyas → Kakatiyas → Reddis → Vijayanagara**; **Kesari Samudra** (Kesamudram) lake = Kakatiya **Prola I**.

r: Three Shiva temples at **Kalidindi** for fallen Chola soldiers

4.x: **Vengi school:** Vesara/Chalukya idiom; **local sandstone (not granite)**, raised jagati; it leads into the **Chalukya-Chola** style.
**Shaivism dominant** (Kapalika, Kalamukha, Pasupata sects); mother goddess **Hariti**; tolerant of Jainism and Buddhism.

r: Built the Jain **Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati / Nedumbasadi** at **Vijayawada** – recorded in the **Musinikonda grant**
The Eastern Chalukya king who **embraced Jainism** (guru **Trikalayogi Siddhanti**; Ramatirtha cave)

4.x: **Dynasty that most propagated Jainism in Telugu land = the Vemulawada Chalukyas** – patrons of **Pampa** and Somadeva Suri; Baddega built the Subhadhama Jinalaya.

5.x: **Title Narendra Mrigaraja ("lion among kings") = Vijayaditya II**; his other titles: Chalukya Rama, Vikramadhavala.

**108 Shiva temples – the Narendreswara / Narendra Mrigeswara-alayas = Vijayaditya II** – built **as penance** at the sites of his **108 battles in 12 years** with the Rashtrakutas (Govinda III, Amoghavarsha).

r: Overthrew his brother **Bhima Salki** and took the throne (c. 808/818)
